items.title: Father Al Lewis Interview, 1972-02-21
items.q: He taught me banjo, he taught Kimball's banjo, he taught Sales's banjo.

ctx.x: He taught me banjo. He taught me banjo, he taught Kimball's banjo, he taught Sales's banjo. But I was the last one that he taught. How old were you then? Well that's where I got the figure out. And Philip Boito, you know, got the music still down there. I took, when Willie Foster went back to St. Louis, he played up there. Well, we still worked for St. Louis, you know, the Boots used to leave town and go up there. Well, I got another teacher, he was at GC Coins, he was on Cronley Street then. Philip Boito, he…
What did Willie Foster teach you? How did he teach you the language?
